Everything here has a working default. Open it only if you want to tune how the selector measures and switches.
Comma-separated country codes, empty means any. Uses the country found by the IP test, so profiles that were never IP-tested are skipped while this is set.
How many profiles are loaded into the running config. The selector switches between these instantly, with no reconnect. Higher costs more memory and startup time.
Hard ceiling on how many profiles are measured and kept in the ranked list. When every running profile dies, replacements are taken from this list.

URL test results this recent are reused instead of being measured again — including tests you ran yourself on the group, so starting the selector right after one does not repeat the work. Older results are treated as if the profile had never been tested. Set to zero to always run a fresh test.

Keeps servers whose last test failed out of the pool, as long as that result is still within the trust window. Turn off if your tests are unreliable and you would rather let the selector decide for itself.
How many profiles are kept confirmed working at all times, so a failure can be covered instantly. These are also the ones traffic is shared between when balancing is on.
The top-ranked profiles are re-checked every interval. The rest are still checked, just spread over the slower full sweep.
How often the closely-checked profiles are measured again.
How long one pass over every running profile takes. Checks are spread evenly across it, so a large pool never causes a burst of traffic.

How often the profile currently carrying your traffic is checked on its own. Keep this short: a server can stop working while still accepting connections, and nothing else would notice until the next full check.
Ranking uses the average and the jitter over this many recent checks, so a single bad result cannot demote a good server.
Another profile must be at least this much faster before the selector moves to it. Higher values mean fewer switches.
Profiles slower than this are never selected, even if nothing better is available.
When the chosen profile fails to connect, how many others to try immediately before the app sees an error.

Applies when the selector switches because a profile got worse or failed. On: everything moves to the new profile at once. Off: current downloads finish on the old one. Balance rotations never drop connections either way.
How long the selector stays on one profile before moving to the next ready one.
The best profile carries all traffic; the other ready profiles are kept verified so one can take over instantly.
New connections move to another good profile on each rotation; open ones are left alone and finish where they started. Traffic is counted exactly.
Every new connection may take a different profile. Widest spread, but your exit IP changes mid-session and per-profile traffic becomes approximate.
Fetched through each profile to measure it. Leave empty to use the global latency test URL.

Fetched WITHOUT the proxy to tell a dead internet connection apart from dead servers, and to notice the moment it comes back. Leave empty to inherit \"Direct test URL\" from Settings › Testing, and empty there too to rely on the system\'s network state. A URL that turns out to be blocked can only delay a resume by a few minutes; it can never keep the selector paused.
